title: Approval roles and separation-of-duties policy
description: Which roles may submit, approve and revise accounting revisions, whether a second approver is required, and how v1 user roles map onto the spec section 13.2 roles. Spec WF02 (submit validates permissions in one transaction; approve requires a different approver with current authorization), WF05 (roles and scope enforced on every API, job, export and socket), section 13.2 role table. Decision D06 (submitter != approver, one approver). Consumed by sub-phase 2.8 (`RolesGuard` + lifecycle commands) and 0.4 (global guards, legacy mapping).

submitRoles.description: Roles allowed to save draft lines, request recompute and `submit` a revision (ACC10, WF02).

approveRoles.description: Roles allowed to `approve` or `reject` an in-review revision (WF01, WF02).

reviseRoles.description: Roles allowed to open a revision of an approved period (`revise`, WF04); 'Unlock' in the UI maps here.

requireTwoApprovers.description: When true a revision needs two distinct approvers (both != submitter) before it becomes `approved` (D06 question 1).

forbidSelfApproval.description: Always true: the submitter may never approve their own revision, whatever their roles, including legacy SuperAdmin (WF02, T36). Present so the rule is visible and recorded with the policy version.

legacyRoleMap.description: v1 `users.role` value -> granted section 13.2 roles, used until identities carry the new roles (0.4). Keys are the seven legacy role names; every key must be present so no legacy user is silently unmapped.
